raw_response:
I only have 1.5 mu, and this year I will still plant cotton on all of it. I have done cotton for years, and on such a small plot I know the field well. Cotton takes more hand work than maize, but for my family this is still manageable, especially since some of us can help at key times even though a few people work off-farm. I am not planning anything fancy. I will plant in mid to late April, use a hybrid cotton seed that people around here commonly buy, put most fertilizer on before or at planting, and then add a smaller topdressing later if the plants are growing weak. Water comes from the well, so I cannot irrigate too freely because pumping costs money, but cotton still needs a few timely irrigations if spring is dry or during flowering and boll setting. For pests, I will not spray just because of fear; I will watch the field and spray when I see aphids or bollworm pressure getting serious. On a small field like mine, spending too much on inputs is not worth it, but spending too little is also risky because if the stand is poor or the bolls set badly, I lose the whole year's income from this plot. So I will manage it in the usual local way, a bit on the safe side, not the highest-input way.
